entries.title: Approval integrity is underspecified
entries.description: The spec says promotion requires an approved proposal, but it does not define whether approval is bound to the exact proposal content that was reviewed. A proposal could be approved, later appended with new evidence or modified by dedupe, and then promoted under an old approval. That breaks the safety claim that operator approval gates the actual artifact being promoted.

entries.title: Model reviewer access is not constrained enough
entries.description: The spec says the model reviewer is optional and receives redacted bundles, but it does not define a strict tool sandbox or execution boundary. Under adversarial logs, a model reviewer could be implemented in a normal agent context with filesystem, shell, Notion, Slack, or memory write access. The design stance explicitly wanted scoped reviewer access, but the current spec only constrains prompts and output paths, not available tools.

entries.title: Install and update behavior lacks conflict semantics
entries.description: The spec requires fresh installs and additive updates, but it does not say how managed files are identified, versioned, or merged when an existing installed root has local edits to the same workflow, command, skill, or config path. Without a managed-file manifest or conflict policy, implementation could overwrite operator configuration while still claiming to be additive. This is especially risky because the feature is explicitly default-installed.

entries.title: Score dimensions are named but not operationalized
entries.description: Scoring is described as deterministic, but dimensions such as severity, reuse, confidence, blast radius, and staleness still lack concrete mappings from evidence to 0-5 values. Different implementers could produce incompatible scores and churn behavior while satisfying the prose. This weakens the threshold guarantee because total >= 18 is only meaningful if the score rubric is stable.

entries.title: Path allowlist needs symlink and traversal rules
entries.description: The spec says every write checks target paths against output_paths, but it does not define canonicalization, symlink handling, or ancestor directory creation rules. A malicious or corrupted installed root could place symlinks under the allowed self-improvement directories that redirect writes into live shared surfaces or source files. A string-prefix allowlist would pass while violating the no-live-mutation invariant.

entries.title: Proposal mutation rules are incomplete
entries.description: Dedupe can append evidence to an active proposal, approve/reject can update status, and promotion can update state, but the spec does not define atomic writes, file locking, or concurrent scheduled/manual runs. A scheduled apply and manual approval could race, producing partial YAML, lost evidence, or approvals against mid-write content. This matters because the feature explicitly supports both scheduled and on-demand execution.

entries.title: External source authorization is vague
entries.description: External evidence is disabled by default, but the spec does not define what proves a source is explicitly configured and authorized or how credentials are kept out of evidence bundles. A future implementation could treat any locally available connector or environment token as authorization. That would conflict with the stated privacy and Notion workspace constraints.

entries.title: Root path examples conflict with canonical paths
entries.description: The spec says source templates install under harness/shared_factory, while some evidence examples still refer to shared_factory/06-runs-and-logs without the harness prefix. It also says older top-level shared_factory roots are legacy input roots only. The mixed wording could cause tests or docs to accidentally read or write the wrong tree.
